label: HStack
title: HStack
summary: Use HStack for a row of related content. It owns horizontal rhythm, alignment, and optional wrapping while the host decides how much room the row has.
corePrinciple: Keep related actions and values in one visual row. Let the available container decide when a wrapped row needs a second line.

anatomy.title: HStack has one job
anatomy.description: See the row, slot, rhythm, and cross-axis behavior in one live example.
blocks: Children are arranged left to right. Reverse changes visual direction only; DOM order stays the same.
Use Slot gap to set rhythm. Keep spacing owned by HStack instead of adding child margins.
Figma exposes the variant named “Aligment”: Top Left maps to the top edge and Left centers the row vertically.
Default supplies the inset around the slot. Use None when the surrounding owner already supplies that edge.

configuration.title: Configure the owner, then read the result
configuration.description: Choose the row rhythm and constraint. Alignment supports the row; it does not replace content hierarchy.
blocks: Use XS through XL to set the rhythm of one row. The gap belongs to the HStack owner.
Default gives the row its component inset. None is useful when the host already owns the edge.
Keep one owner for the inset
Wrapping needs a constrained width. Alignment changes the cross-axis position; it never changes row direction.
Let the host provide the constraint
Surface intent comes from the owner
HStack and its children inherit the selected Coin mode context. Keep color mode and stack context consistent with the surrounding public component.

states.title: HStack responds to its host
states.description: Compare default, changed rhythm, host-owned edge, and constrained outcomes without recreating the layout primitive.
blocks: HStack uses its default direction and token rhythm.
Changing the owner gap changes the whole group.
None lets a containing pattern own the edge inset.
Wrapping appears when the host supplies a constraint.
A stack is a layout result inside its parent. Make the container boundary and content order clear before changing gap or wrap.

sizing.title: The parent supplies the constraint
sizing.description: HStack wrap is a width outcome. Keep the parent boundary meaningful before enabling it.
blocks: HStack can wrap when its width is constrained. DOM order remains stable.

content.title: Make the relationship visible
content.description: Rows work when siblings are related by one decision or task.
blocks: Use HStack when items belong to one row and should share a rhythm.
Reverse changes visual order while assistive technology still follows the DOM order.
Wrap needs a meaningful parent width. Avoid a row that can spill beyond its owner.
Populate public component slots with HStack instead of recreating child margins.

inContext.title: Place the primitive where the relationship happens
inContext.description: Use HStack for related siblings that belong on one row or wrap as one group.
blocks: Pair a value, status, and action when they describe one decision.
A narrow card can wrap the row once there is a real width boundary.
Make the row do one job
Use a horizontal stack for related siblings, not unrelated page sections.

doDont.title: Protect structure and clarity
doDont.description: These pairs keep the layout relationship visible as content and host constraints change.
blocks: Wrap inside a real width boundary
The host makes available width visible and the row can continue on a second line.
Let children spill out of the owner
A row without a width constraint can overflow and lose its relationship to the parent.
Let the host own the edge inset
The visible boundary has one clear owner and the content remains aligned.
Stack component insets without a reason
Nested owners can create an unintended double edge and weaken alignment.

sources.title: Grounded in the published component
sources.description: The guide separates designer choices from behavior supplied by the public library at runtime.
blocks: Live layout examples use public exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. HStack uses its public package export with token-driven modes; documentation controls change owner configuration, not component internals.
